title: A Lean formalization of dual-sourcing submodularity and optimal-order existence
contribution_type: Two complete Lean formalizations of established mathematical statements

owner.source_commit_scope: Completed owning-project editorial record and its detailed lifecycle; the owning repository remains private.

claim: For the exact two-supplier random-capacity model, expected profit is lattice-submodular in feasible orders. With absolutely continuous demand, a global maximizing nonnegative order exists and each coordinate is zero, its design capacity, or has an existing zero partial derivative.

assumptions.suppliers: Two suppliers, indexed by Fin 2; positive finite design capacities.
assumptions.cost_parameters: 0 <= eta_i <= 1; r, p, c_i >= 0; v < r+p. These include disclosed platform additions.
assumptions.capacity_laws: For each reliability index, nonnegative atomless probability laws; CDF monotonicity in reliability is retained in Model.
assumptions.joint_law: The two capacity losses and demand are independent, through the exact product measure.
assumptions.demand_both_targets: A probability law on the real line, nonnegative almost surely, with integrable identity.
assumptions.demand_theorem_1_only: Absolute continuity with respect to Lebesgue measure.
assumptions.feasible_orders: All componentwise nonnegative real vectors; no upper order cap is assumed.
assumptions.source_correspondence: The packet proves the complete platform signatures. The finite-mean and parameter qualifications supplied by the platform are disclosed; no equivalence to a broader unstated source theorem is claimed.
